correctness.rationale: For any block duration t, integrating the exponential Poisson amplitude gives bilateral geometric lattice masses c_t q_t^|j| and F_t(z)=[1+lambda_bar*t(1-(z+z^-1)/2)]^-1. A stationary elapsed uniform phase U makes an integer n-period observation comprise n−1 whole blocks and independent partial blocks (1−U), U; direct integration yields 2 log(h)/[h^(n−1)(h²−1)] with h=1+B[1−(z+z^-1)/2]. Near unique outer singularity z=q^-1, h=c^-1(1−qz)+higher terms, giving 2q^m/m at n=1 and 2c^(n−1)m^(n−2)log(m)q^m/(n−2)! for n≥2. For n+α, 0<α<1, split U at 1−α: n full-block sector contributes order h^-n times J_α=2 log(1/(1−α))/(2−α); the other sector has at most order h^-(n−1)log h. For n=1, endpoint layer U=w/m gives conditional likelihood c q^m exp(−cw) and symmetric endpoints. For n≥2, n−1 complete block geometric convolutions under the q^-m tilt and partial tilted increments at u in [m^-b,m^-a] give fixed-phase local mass c^(n−1)m^(n−2)q^m/((n−2)!u(1−u)); integrating du/u over log-scale intervals and dividing by full log(m) mass produces independent uniform log exponent and fair endpoint label. Infinite statements rest on analytic pole/singularity/convolution comparisons, not finite tests. Independent FFT Laurent contour calculations used an independently integrated two-sector noninteger generating function and checked n=1,2,3, α=0,0.3,0.4,0.35 and B=0.2,1,5; direct geometric-pole likelihood quadrature corroborated both phase limits at m=100,300,1000. Boundary parameters B>0,n fixed positive,α strictly in (0,1); zero-duration limit and joint near-integer boundary-layer scaling are not claimed.

originality.rationale: Direct statement-to-statement comparison distinguishes this stationarily random-phase, exponentially refreshed Cox lattice walk from the directly antecedent aligned-initialization model and from generic renewal CTRW large-deviation studies. The antecedent fixes the rate-block boundary at the observation origin and supplies the one-block transform, but neither the uniform-phase logarithmic generating function nor the sharp integer/noninteger exact lattice prefactors and extreme-displacement conditional phase. A separate 2022 fixed-time large-displacement paper does treat tail prefactors and logarithmic corrections, but presupposes independent waiting times; it does not imply this temporally correlated fixed-period Cox model or the latent-phase law. The Resultary semantic searches did not return a directly covering statement. This is a bounded, best-of-knowledge originality assessment, not proof of historical priority.

value.rationale: For a deterministically refreshed stochastic-intensity environment, uniform random phase is the canonical observation-time stationary law. The theorem classifies exact fixed-time rare-displacement lattice prefactors over every integer and strictly noninteger refresh ratio, showing a sharp logarithmic/arithmetic resonance not recoverable from Gaussian or mean-square transport results. Its two distinct conditional hidden-clock distributions quantify which unobserved refresh alignments dominate rare events. These are natural asymptotic and inference invariants for the model, not arbitrary finite slices, routine reparameterizations, or a known-table recomputation; the result does not claim broader intensity priors or code/experiment guarantees.

limitations: Analytic asymptotics hold at fixed B>0, tau>0, integer n>=1 and alpha in (0,1), m tending to positive infinity, stationary phase initialization, exponential independent rate redraws and ±1 jumps.
No uniform joint limit as alpha approaches 0 or 1 with growing m, other rate distributions, nonstationary alignment, first-passage laws, or actual finite-data identifiability is proved.
Numerical contour and quadrature checks are bounded corroboration of a reconstructed analytic proof, not formal infinite certificates.
No expert attestation, Lean proof, or certified exhaustive priority search.
